title: The supper of the Lamb (Apocalypse 19:6–9)
hook: blessed are they that are called: echoed at every Mass

segments.voice: Yesterday, Babylon falls, in one hour, and the merchants weep. Your line was what doesn't last. What did you skip buying, and where did it go instead? Day six hundred twenty-nine.

Alleluia is sung at Mass all year, except in Lent. It's in hymns, on Easter cards, in the names of choirs. Now look for it in the Apocalypse. In chapter nineteen it comes four times, close together. Right after Babylon falls, the noise of the merchants weeping is drowned out by another sound. John hears what sounds like a great crowd, like many waters, like great thunders, and they're shouting alleluia. Then they say why. There's going to be a wedding.
screen: `ALLELUIA, ALL YEAR LONG.` → `FOUR TIMES IN APOCALYPSE NINETEEN.` → `THERE'S GOING TO BE A WEDDING.`

segments.voice: The crowd sings that the Lord God Almighty reigns. Let us be glad and rejoice, they say, for the marriage of the Lamb has come, and his bride has made herself ready. She's given fine linen to wear, bright and clean, and the text explains the linen: it's the good deeds of the saints. So the bride is the Church, God's people, dressed in the love they've lived. Babylon was the city dressed in purple and scarlet, bought and sold. The bride is dressed in deeds. Then an angel tells John to write something down. In the Douay-Rheims: "Blessed are they that are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb." And the angel adds: these are the true words of God. Again and again in the Bible, God's love for his people is pictured as a marriage, from the prophets to Jesus's parable of the wedding feast. Here that picture becomes a feast. Now here's where Catholics hear it. At every Mass, just before Communion, the priest holds up the host and says, behold the Lamb of God. And then he says that those called to the supper of the Lamb are blessed. In Latin the line is beati qui ad cenam Agni vocati sunt: blessed are those called to the supper of the Lamb. The people answer with the words of a centurion from Matthew's Gospel: Lord, I am not worthy that thou shouldst enter under my roof: but only say the word, as the Douay-Rheims gives it. Called, and not worthy, and coming anyway. The Church teaches that every Mass is a foretaste of this wedding feast.
screen: `ALLELUIA: THE LORD REIGNS.` · `THE BRIDE DRESSED IN DEEDS.` · `WRITE IT DOWN: BLESSED ARE THEY.` · `BEHOLD THE LAMB, AT EVERY MASS.` · then, large: `BLESSED ARE THEY THAT ARE CALLED.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: hear it ahead of time. Sit comfortably and breathe. Picture the moment at Mass just before Communion: the priest lifting the host, the quiet in the church, the words, behold the Lamb of God. Then the line about those who are called to the supper. Imagine hearing it as an invitation with your name on it, to a wedding feast that is already being set. Notice what comes up. If you pray, you can answer in the centurion's words, Lord, I am not worthy, but only say the word. If you don't, just sit with being invited. The bell holds the time.
Cenam Agni. Latin for the supper of the Lamb, the words said at every Mass just before Communion is offered. Today's word.
Your line: called to the supper. Today, when someone invites you anywhere, even for coffee, let it remind you of the other invitation. Day six hundred twenty-nine.

howItsDone: Before Communion at every Mass, the priest shows the host and says Behold the Lamb of God, adding that those called to the supper of the Lamb are blessed; the people respond with the centurion's words, Lord, I am not worthy, and the Church teaches that the Eucharist anticipates the wedding feast of the Lamb.

original.say: beh-AH-tee kwee ahd CHAY-nahm AH-nyee vo-KAH-tee soont
original.note: Latin: blessed are those called to the supper of the Lamb, said at Mass before Communion (Apocalypse 19:9).

trapdoor: what you thought: a nice line the priest says before Communion.
what it means: the invitation to the wedding feast of Christ and his people, which every Mass already tastes.
what a scholar hears: alleluia four times in 19:1–6; the bride's linen is 'the justifications of saints'; the Mass line quotes 19:9.

notes: Editor review (2026-10-01): removed the 'only in Apocalypse 19' superlative (hook, match, myth, trapdoor) and the 2011-translation date; 'Roman' centurion trimmed to the text's 'centurion'; Matthew 8:8 added as a quoted Douay source; practice no longer names the listener's feelings; carry task changed so it doesn't repeat day 625's Mass carry.
Alleluia appears in the New Testament only in Apocalypse 19:1, 3, 4, 6. Confirm.
Apocalypse 19:8: Douay-Rheims 'the fine linen are the justifications of saints'; paraphrased as 'the good deeds of the saints'. Confirm.

The Mass's invitation and response are paraphrased, not quoted from the 2011 English Missal (not public domain); the Latin 'Beati qui ad cenam Agni vocati sunt' is quoted. Confirm the 2011 change note (earlier English: 'Happy are those who are called to his supper').
Alleluia omitted during Lent: confirm phrasing 'sung at Mass all year, except in Lent'.
